en: The Chapter on Similes, Part One: The Lion Section.
6. The Question of the Hundred-Winged Bird “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one quality of the hundred-winged bird should be adopted,’ which is that one quality that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, the hundred-winged bird, having cried out, announces to others either safety or danger;”
"In the same way, Great King, a yogi practicing yoga who teaches the Dhamma to others should show the states of deprivation as fearful and Nibbāna as secure.
This, Great King, is one quality that should be adopted from the hundred-petaled lotus.
And this, Great King, was said by the elder Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja:"
both of these are matters of consequence.”
This is the sixth question, on the hundred-petaled lotus.
